newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa stable after surgery success.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa stable after surgery success.

text.p: Mother Teresa was stable but still in danger on Saturday after life-saving surgery to clear two coronary artery blockages, her doctors said.
"Mother had a peaceful night. She is stable but not out of danger," said a regular medical bulletin, issued by the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in the Indian city of Calcutta.

The 86-year-old nun, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her devotion to the poor, on Friday underwent angiography and angioplasty for the third time since 1991. Nuns at the Calcutta headquarters of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity order said its members worldwide would hold special prayers for her on Saturday.
The Roman Catholic order, with about 4,500 nuns in more than 80 countries, was founded by Mother Teresa in 1949.
After Friday's surgery, an American doctor on Mother Teresa's team at the Birla clinic said angioplasty had saved the life of the 1979 Nobel Peace prize winner.
Doctor Patricia Aubanel said some danger remained to her heart and it would take her up to three months to recover.
"She was going to have a heart attack -- a major heart attack -- if the angioplasty was not done," she told reporters.
"Mother could not have left the hospital alive without this angioplasty," said Aubanel, who treated Mother Teresa in California in 1991.
Angiography is an X-ray test which uses an injected opaque dye to show up blocked arteries. Angioplasty is the procedure to unblock the artery by inserting a balloon and inflating it.
The procedures were performed eight days after Mother Teresa entered hospital with an irregular heartbeat.
She was fitted with a pacemaker in 1989.
A medical bulletin issued after the angioplasty said the angiogram had shown "blockages in two major coronary arteries".
"Many complications can still arise and her irregular heart rhythm still continues to be a problem," it said.
Dr D.P. Shetty, who led the surgical team, said angioplasty could be repeated, if necessary.
"We were fully prepared and in case of an emergency we are ready for surgery. I was sure she would recover, although statistically the risks are very high," he said.
Mother Teresa previously had angiography and angioplasty in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993.
"She surprises everybody," Aubanel said on Friday. "She has amazing records of speedy recovery. At least on four earlier occasions she was nearly dead, but every time she recovered."

Doctors said Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, had suffered heart failure several times since entering the Woodlands Nursing Home in Calcutta on November 22. She was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday.
